findings.interpretation: Most recorded entry requests were rejected while the entry state machine was not armed; candidates were nevertheless created in both arms.
limits: The historical run does not preserve a complete candidate-to-policy-choice trace.
Counts do not distinguish mask, policy, decoder, candidate-lifetime, and FSM-contract causes.
Counts do not explain the economic outcome.

findings.interpretation: At retained fill timestamps, midpoint PnL is positive for both arms while recorded executable bid/ask PnL is negative.
limits: This is a fixed-fill accounting decomposition, not a cost intervention or a deployable midpoint result.
Fill-to-source alignment finds 16 changed-quote timestamp groups and 87 missing-side groups among 3,698 events; parser carry/grid match does not prove quote availability or broker execution.
Unknown provider clock and equal-timestamp row order limit interpretation of selected quote rows.

findings.interpretation: The saved March-to-April gross mean-R change intervals include zero for both arms; entry-cohort and conditional EMA21-exit components do not identify a separated cause.
limits: The EMA21 reference is conditional on historical entries and is not a causal policy or account-path counterfactual.
This is not a full-year mechanism analysis.

findings.interpretation: Recorded PPO metrics are finite after the first dashboard row; sampled losses, entropy, KL, clip fraction, and explained-variance values do not establish effective learning.
limits: No gradient-norm or constrained-PPO dual/cost updates are recorded in training_log.csv.
Dashboard gradient norms and zero cost/breach values are 21 sampled snapshots, not continuous history.
No predeclared metric acceptance thresholds establish stability.
Parser reconstruction does not establish source row chronology, provider clock, order-arrival availability, or broker execution.
The 87 carried-side events and 16 changed-quote events retain source chronology uncertainty.

findings.interpretation: These counts limit executable-price interpretation but do not identify which prices a historical policy could have received.
